problem: The chapter says cost and work "carry different units, so do not compare them directly", but the efficiency formula given three lines earlier is exactly the comparison of the two: E = T₁ ÷ (p × Tₚ) = work ÷ cost. A student reading both statements will be confused about whether work and cost may be divided.
fix: Say instead: cost C = p × Tₚ is in processor-seconds and work W = T₁ is in seconds; their ratio is dimensionless and is exactly the efficiency, E = W ÷ C = T₁ ÷ (p × Tₚ). When E < 1, part of the cost buys no useful work.

where: Section 2 (step from the time bound to Amdahl's law)
problem: "Divide T₁ by both sides" is ambiguous; it reads as dividing the number T₁ by two sides rather than dividing T₁ by each side of the inequality.
fix: Write: "Divide T₁ by both sides of the inequality. The left side becomes T₁ ÷ Tₚ, which is S, so S ≤ 1 ÷ (f + (1 − f) ÷ p)."

problem: The same symbol f is used twice with different meanings: the serial fraction of the one-processor time in Amdahl's law, and the serial fraction of the parallel run in Gustafson's law. Students will carry f = 0.1 from Amdahl straight into S′ = f + p(1 − f) and get a wrong answer.
fix: Use a different symbol for the scaled case, for example S′ = f_G + p(1 − f_G), and state plainly: f_G is the serial fraction of the parallel run's time, and f_G ≠ f in general.

problem: The roofline model does not plot achieved speedup. It plots attained floating-point performance (FLOP/s) against arithmetic intensity (FLOP per byte), bounded by peak floating-point rate and by memory bandwidth.
fix: Write: "the roofline model, which plots attained performance against arithmetic intensity and shows whether the peak floating-point rate or memory bandwidth is the binding limit".
